title: pprof: CPU, memory, blocking and goroutines

videos.script: A program is slow, and you have a guess about why. This lesson replaces the guess with a measurement. {{kinds}} Go's runtime can record several kinds of profile. The CPU profile looks at what is running, a hundred times a second. The heap profile notes which code allocates memory. Others list every goroutine, or the time spent waiting for a lock. Two of them stay off until you turn them on. {{bench}} Then three ways to get one. From a benchmark, with two flags to go test. {{program}} From a program of your own, with a handful of calls to the runtime pprof package. {{server}} And from a process that is already running, over HTTP, without stopping it. That last one finds a goroutine leak in a small service, and a one-line change fixes it. {{close}} The workload is the tally package from lesson one, counting two million log lines. All three ways point at the same function. This lesson collects the profiles and takes a first look. Reading one properly is lesson thirteen.
